Supplementary Affidavit filed in Court is taken  on record.
The petitioner is an unfortunate father of a  woman who died on 10th April, 2024 in the house of her  in-laws.
On the complaint lodged by the petitioner an  F.I.R. being no. 246/24 dated 10th April, 2024 was  registered under Sections 498A/306/34 I.P.C.
The petitioner submits that her daughter was  murdered for not meeting up the demand of dowry of  her in-laws.
The body of her daughter was not handed  over to the petitioner.

sentences.text:
The other daughters of the petitioner i.e. the sisters of  the deceased who were present in front of the  postmortem room, were taken into custody and a  2 proceeding has been initiated against them being Murshidabad P.S. Case No. 695/24 dated 10th April,
2024 under Sections 151/107 Cr.P.C.

The petitioner submits that the in-laws of her daughter are extremely influential persons and they are threatening the petitioner and his family members with dire consequences if steps are taken to proceed with any complaint with regard to the incident of death of his daughter.
It has been submitted that there are CCTV camera installed at the matrimonial house of the deceased but the police has not taken any steps to collect evidence from the same.
The investigation is being conducted in a perfunctory manner.
The petitioner prays for a direction for handing over the investigation to the Criminal Investigation Department.

Learned Advocate representing the State respondents submits, upon instruction that, a case has already been registered on the death of the daughter of the petitioner and the same is being proceeded with in the proper manner.

sentences.text: As regards the query put forth by the Court on 15th May, 2024 with regard to the videography of the postmortem examination, it has been submitted that videography has not been made.
It has further been submitted that in the course of investigation it has been revealed that the CCTV cameras installed in the house of the husband of the deceased were non functional.

From the submission made on behalf of the parties and upon perusal of the materials placed before this Court, it appears that the petitioner is apprehending serious threat in the hands of the in-laws of his deceased daughter.
More than two months have expired from the date of death of his daughter but the investigation does not appear to have proceeded much.

Though it has been submitted that the husband of the deceased was arrested immediately, but even thereafter the petitioner is receiving telephonic threats on regular basis desisting him from proceeding further with the subject case.
Apprehension has been disclosed before the Court with regard to the tampering of evidence.
Accordingly, the Court thinks it fit to direct the concerned investigating officer to hand over all the documents in relation to the instant case to the Additional Director of Police, C.I.D.
The Criminal Investigation Department is directed to proceed with the investigation in a diligent manner and try to reach at its logical conclusion at the earliest.

In the event the petitioner continues to receive any further threat in the hands of the in-laws of the deceased or from their men and agents, it will be open for the petitioner to lodge appropriate complaint before the Superintendent of Police, Murshidabad who shall immediately respond to the same.
The proceeding in connection with the Murshidabad P.S. Case No.695/24 dated 10th April, 2024 registered against the sisters of the deceased is directed to be stayed for the time being.
Let the matter appear in the list on 15th July, 2024 and an updated report be produced by the learned advocate for the State on the adjourned date.

Learned Advocate representing the State respondents submits that the case diary could not be produced today as the matter appear in the list on the preponed date on the prayer made by the learned advocate representing the petitioner.
Prayer has been made to permit the respondents to produce the case diary on the adjourned date.
Let the case diary be produced on the adjourned date.

(Amrita Sinha, J.)
